answer.answer:
Compared the pescatarian diet with the two closest fish-based, plant-forward diets on Healthline for healthier eating:

1) Pescatarian diet (healthline.com/nutrition/pescatarian-diet): a vegetarian eating pattern that excludes red meat and poultry but includes fish and other seafood; it is largely plant-based (whole grains, legumes, nuts, seeds, fruits, vegetables, healthy fats) and may include dairy and eggs. Healthline reports pescatarians had lower diabetes risk (4.8% vs 7.6% in omnivores), ~22% lower risk of dying from heart disease, and women gained ~2.5 lb less per year; it supplies omega-3s (EPA/DHA from oily fish) plus protein, vitamin B12, zinc and selenium. Watch mercury in large fish (limit tilefish, swordfish, shark, king mackerel; limit albacore/yellowfin tuna). Fish-eater diets caused 46% fewer greenhouse-gas emissions than daily meat-eaters.

2) Mediterranean diet (healthline.com/nutrition/mediterranean-diet-meal-plan): the fish-forward, plant-based pattern closest to pescatarian — high in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, legumes, nuts/seeds and healthy fats (olive oil), low in animal products/meat, with fish/seafood at least twice a week; limits processed foods, added sugar, refined grains and alcohol, with no calorie restriction. It may help with weight, heart health and diabetes risk, and the American Heart Association ranks it Tier 1 (score >85) for heart health — the same top tier as the pescatarian and vegetarian diets.

Comparison / bottom line: Both are plant-forward, fish-based and top-rated for heart health. The pescatarian diet is the stricter 'vegetarian + fish' pattern (no red meat/poultry; dairy and eggs optional) and is more flexible and easier to follow than vegan/vegetarian while supplying DHA/EPA; the Mediterranean diet is a broader, flexible lifestyle pattern that allows small amounts of poultry/red meat and is the most-studied overall. For eating healthier, both are excellent — choose pescatarian if you want a meat-free, fish-based plan, or Mediterranean if you want flexibility with proven heart benefits. Healthline's own comparison (Vegetarian vs. Vegan vs. Pescatarian) adds that all three exclude red meat/poultry and emphasize nutrient-dense plant foods, with pescatarian the most flexible and vegan the most restrictive (may need B12/iron supplements).
